user_message: A bar magnet falls more slowly through a copper pipe than through a plastic pipe. Explain why, and predict what changes if the copper pipe has a slit along its length.
allowed_evidence: Changing magnetic flux through a conductor induces electric fields and currents. By Lenz's law, the induced magnetic effect opposes the change producing it. A longitudinal slit interrupts many closed circumferential current paths.
public_rubric: Connects motion, changing flux, induced currents, and force.
Predicts the slit-pipe outcome with a reason.
Mentions where the lost mechanical energy goes.
